Soojin / team — quick technical triage below. TL;DR: We can produce a limited evidence pack this week and propose a time-bound exception for BYOK in the target region, with follow-up engineering work for a full BYOK flow.

1) BYOK / KMS support
- Private deployments: we currently support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for on-prem and selected VPC regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1). If MedTechPlus's deployment is in one of those regions we can do full BYOK now.
- If they require a different region: we _do not_ have an automated cross-region BYOK onboarding flow yet. Option: time-bound exception where we provision a dedicated KMS instance under Redwood control, generate attestation artifacts (KMS policy, access logs), and sign an operational control attestation. This requires a security review + PS runbook (~5 business days) but we can provide an attestation letter and configuration screenshots in 48–72 hours.

2) Audit logs retention/export
- We can configure retention windows up to 3 years in the current private runtime without code changes; 7 years requires long-term storage (cold export) which is a new capability.
- Short-term approach: we can export daily audit-log bundles to an S3 bucket owned by MedTechPlus (encrypted, versioned) for indefinite retention. That export pipeline is supported today in a manual/ops-assisted way; we can operationalize it with a simple automation (Glue/lambda) in ~7–10 business days.
- Evidence: we can pull redacted sample logs and the runtime logging pipeline diagram for them to review.

3) Evidence pack and artifacts we can deliver in 48–72 hours (without infra changes):
- SOC2-compliant control descriptions + relevant sections (redacted)
- Sample, redacted audit logs (token-levels removed)
- Architecture diagram for Private with KMS and logging (static PNG)
- Proposed exception attestation letter draft (security-signed)

Constraints / blockers:
- Exporting raw logs to an external customer bucket requires a signed data transfer agreement and PS time to configure IAM/SC policy; timeline depends on procurement for dedicated capacity and network setup.
- Any attestation referencing KMS key material must avoid exposing key material; we can provide policies, configuration, and KMS-access logs only.

Next steps I suggest:
- Approve short-term exception + evidence pack to unblock procurement this week. Marcus to produce artifacts and coordinate with Security for attestation.
- Kickoff a small product spike to add an automated export/retention flow for 7yr retention (roadmap item).

I'll start assembling the artifacts once we confirm to proceed.

—Marcus
